RESULT 06/08/26

Implementation: API Share

Route

POST /posts/share
Authorization: <JWT token>
Content-Type: application/json

Payload

{
  "sid": "post-slug"
}

Behavior

  • Only authenticated user sessions may record a share.
  • Only published, non-private posts may be shared.
  • Each (user_id, post_id) pair is stored once.
  • A new share returns exist: false; a repeated request returns exist: true.
  • The response includes the current PostgreSQL counter_share.
  • Elasticsearch counter_share updates only after a new share is created, while existing counters are preserved.
  • Viewer shares and share destinations are out of scope.

Success response

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "exist": false,
    "counter_share": 12,
    "messages": "Success Insert Share Post"
  }
}

Error handling

Status Condition
400 Invalid body, missing SID, invalid user ID, or database failure
401 Caller is not an authenticated user
403 Post is private
409 Post is missing or unpublished
500 Elasticsearch connection or update failure

RESULT 06/08/26

Implementation: Create Shares Table

Migration

Added migrations/20260806_create_shares.sql:

CREATE TABLE shares (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    post_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES posts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    CONSTRAINT shares_user_post_key UNIQUE (user_id, post_id)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_shares_post_id ON shares(post_id);

Model

Added Models.Share, mapped to shares, with UUID ID, user and post ownership, timestamps, relations, and the composite unique index metadata.

Constraints

  • Duplicate user-post shares are rejected at database level.
  • User deletion cascades to shares.
  • Post deletion cascades to shares.
  • The post index supports COUNT(*) WHERE post_id = ?.
  • No platform or destination data is stored.

Verification

go vet ./...
git diff --check

Scope

  • Create shares with a UUID primary key.
  • Associate each row with one user and one post.
  • Enforce one row per (user_id, post_id) pair.
  • Cascade-delete share rows when the associated user or post is deleted.
  • Add an index for post share-count queries.
  • Add the corresponding GORM model.

    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),

Implementation: API Add Bookmark

Route

Authorization: <JWT token>
Content-Type: application/json

Changes

  • Changed existing bookmark lookup from (post_id, folder_id, user_id) to (post_id, user_id).
  • Existing bookmarks are deleted by their loaded primary key.
  • New bookmarks still use the validated folder from folder_sid.

  • Added counter_bookmark to the Elasticsearch post counter document.

Data Flow

  1. Validate user, post, folder, visibility, and blocked-post state.
  2. Find bookmark by user and post.
  3. Insert into the selected folder or delete the existing row.

issues.display_title: Issue #434: Update Place List View for Category Filtering
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 07/08/26

✅ Implementation: Update Place List View for Category Filtering

Summary

Updated public.views_place_list with category metadata and latest-post selection required by Home "Places Near You" category filtering.

Migration

Added:

migrations/20260807_update_views_place_list_categories.sql

Updated reference DDL:

docs/migrations/views/DDL_views_place_list.sql

Both files contain the same CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW definition.

Existing Column Compatibility

All existing view columns remain in their original positions:

location_group
location_group_slug
location_name
encrypt
location_post
thumbnail
total_posts
total_views
contributors

New columns are appended:

category_id
category_name
latest_post

This permits CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW without dropping the view or renaming existing columns.

Ranked Post Source

Added a ranked_posts CTE. It joins posts with users, categories, and aggregated views, then ranks posts per place/category:

row_number() OVER (
    PARTITION BY p.location_group, p.category_id
    ORDER BY p.created_at DESC, p.id DESC
) AS place_category_rank

The latest post provides:

  • location_name
  • location_post
  • thumbnail

This prevents one place from splitting into multiple results when posts have different coordinates or thumbnails.

Aggregation Grain

The final view groups by:

rp.location_group,
rp.encrypt,
rp.category_id,
rp.category_name

It does not group by location_post or thumbnail.

This provides one row per place, contributor, and category. GET /places/list performs the final aggregation into one place result after blocked/deactivated contributor filtering.

Category Data

Category data comes from:

LEFT JOIN panorra_dev.public.categories AS c
    ON c.id = p.category_id

The view exposes:

rp.category_id,
rp.category_name

This lets the API filter posts before final place aggregation.

Totals and Contributors

  • total_posts counts matching posts for each place/category/contributor row.
  • total_views sums pre-aggregated post view counts.
  • contributors contains distinct avatar/username objects.
  • latest_post is the latest matching post timestamp.

Filters Preserved

The view includes only:

  • Published posts.
  • Public posts.
  • Non-banned posts.
  • Posts with usable place metadata.
  • Non-banned owners.
  • Owners not pending deletion.

Deployment Status

The corrected migration was applied to the database.

No DROP VIEW is required. Future environments can apply:

migrations/20260807_update_views_place_list_categories.sql

Verification

Verify new fields:

SELECT
    location_group,
    category_id,
    category_name,
    latest_post,
    total_posts,
    total_views
FROM public.views_place_list
LIMIT 10;

Verify the view does not duplicate the same aggregation grain:

SELECT
    location_group,
    category_id,
    encrypt,
    count(*) AS duplicate_rows
FROM public.views_place_list
GROUP BY location_group, category_id, encrypt
HAVING count(*) > 1;

Expected result: no rows.

Objective

Update public.views_place_list to support category-aware Home "Places Near You" results without fragmenting a place by each post's coordinates or thumbnail.

Background

GET /places/list uses views_place_list for place cards and map markers. Home category filtering requires category metadata and a reliable representative post for each place/category combination.

The view must provide:

  • Category identity and name.
  • Latest activity for sorting.
  • One representative location, address, and thumbnail.
  • Correct post/view totals.
  • Contributors.

Requirements

  1. Preserve the view name public.views_place_list.
  2. Use CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW; do not drop the view.
  3. Preserve all existing columns in their current order:
    • location_group
    • location_group_slug
    • location_name
    • encrypt
    • location_post
    • thumbnail
    • total_posts
    • total_views
    • contributors
  4. Append these columns after existing columns:
    • category_id
    • category_name
    • latest_post
  5. Join categories through posts.category_id.
  6. Select representative location_name, location_post, and thumbnail from the latest post for each location_group + category_id.
  7. Do not group directly by location_post or thumbnail.
  8. Count every matching published post once.
  9. Sum view counts for matching posts.
  10. Return distinct contributors.
  11. Preserve visibility and moderation filters.
  12. Exclude users pending deletion.

Representative Post

Rank posts with:

row_number() OVER (
    PARTITION BY p.location_group, p.category_id
    ORDER BY p.created_at DESC, p.id DESC
) AS place_category_rank

issues.display_title: Issue #446: Prevent Zero UUIDs in Notification Inserts
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 14/08/26

? Implementation: Prevent Zero UUIDs in Notification Inserts

Root Cause

The notification models use uuid.UUID primary-key fields. Their create paths constructed model structs without setting ID. GORM serialized the Go zero value into the insert, preventing database defaults from generating UUIDs and causing duplicate primary-key errors.

Changes

  • Added newPushNotification with ID: uuid.New() for mobile Expo-token rows.
  • Added newWebNotification with ID: uuid.New() for web-token rows.
  • Updated TokenNotification create paths to use those initialized models.
  • Added newNotification with ID: uuid.New() for records created by PushNotification.
  • Preserved token lookup/update behavior and notification payload fields.
  • Added regression tests proving all three constructors return non-zero UUIDs.

Audit Result

  • Audited all typed GORM Create calls under src against UUID-primary-key models.
  • The three notification paths above were the affected paths.
  • Other typed UUID creates explicitly assign IDs.
  • Map and raw-SQL inserts that omit id do not send a zero UUID and remain database-default-dependent; they were outside this defect.

Files

  • src/Action/V1/Notifications/TokenNotification.go
  • src/Action/V1/Notifications/TokenNotification_test.go
  • src/Action/V1/Notifications/PushNotification.go
  • src/Action/V1/Notifications/PushNotification_test.go

Verification

go test ./src/Action/V1/Notifications -count=1 -timeout=60s

Git

  • Token registration fix: edbb108
  • Notification record fix: 51b1160

Problem

GORM inserts the zero value of a uuid.UUID primary-key field when a model struct is created without assigning its ID. The database UUID default is not used because the id column is explicitly included as 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000.

This affected notification token registration and notification creation:

  • Mobile push tokens in push_notification.
  • Web push tokens in notifications_web.
  • Notification records created by PushNotification in notifications.

The first zero-UUID insert could succeed; later inserts then failed with a duplicate primary-key violation.

Scope

  • Generate a non-zero UUID before every typed GORM create in the affected notification flows.
  • Cover mobile tokens, web tokens, and notification records.
  • Add focused regression tests for all three constructors.
  • Audit other typed GORM creates using UUID primary keys for the same defect.
  • Do not migrate or clean existing database rows.

Acceptance Criteria

  • New mobile push-token rows never use the zero UUID.
  • New web push-token rows never use the zero UUID.
  • New notification rows from PushNotification never use the zero UUID.
  • Existing update behavior remains unchanged.
  • No other typed GORM UUID create lacking an ID remains in src.
  • Notification tests pass.
